4: The patient's history of perianal fistula, recent mucinous discharge, and pain, combined with the findings of indurated, ulcerative lesions and a well-defined mass at the anorectal junction on CT and MRI, are consistent with mucinous adenocarcinoma. The histological examination of the biopsy specimen also confirmed this diagnosis.

The patient's 12-year history of perianal fistula, recent symptoms, and imaging findings of a mass at the anorectal junction with pelvic lymph node involvement are consistent with anorectal cancer. The diagnosis of mucinous adenocarcinoma further supports this, as it is a subtype of anorectal cancer.
